# Schedule 13D filings: post-filing drift on S&P 100/400/600 names (generated)

**Primary verdict (fund-like filer, 20 sessions, 10 bp/side): `unproven`**. Generated by `scripts/onetime_event_13d_study.py`; interpretation is added by hand below the tables.

Pre-registered in the script docstring: one primary test, a 6-cell grid, filings since 2010, 30-day dedupe, entry at the first close strictly after the acceptance time.

- Initial 13D filings found: 1586; filer name parsed from the cover for 1582; events after dedupe: 1152; fund-like filers: 410.
- Book window 2010-01-05 to 2026-11-06. Alpha is vs QQQ; headline columns at 10 bp/side.
- The filer classifier is a keyword list on the cover-page name, so it is crude: it will call some passive holders 'fund-like' and miss activists with plain names.

## Reading it (hand-written)

**Verdict: `unproven`, tail-driven, not worth building.** The pre-registered primary (fund-like filer, 20 sessions) misses:
t 1.60, same-name placebo p 0.0475, beta 0.68. (A first run that missed 115 post-2024 filer names gave t 1.53, p 0.059; see the parser note below.)

- **The "all filers" books look better and should not be believed.** t 2.3-2.8 and placebo p of 0.0005-0.003, but beta is
  0.76-0.79 (fails the bar), the second half is weak (t 0.5-1.5), and the event-level table shows why: the mean abnormal
  return is +0.4% over 20 sessions with a **median of -0.1%, a 5%-winsorised mean of +0.0% and a 50% win rate**. The
  book holds about five names at a time, so one +200% event moves it. The largest contributors are TGTX (20-session log excess
  return +2.13, about 8x), PARR (+1.43, about 4x), SEZL, MARA, PTGX and GME, all current S&P 600/400 members whose
  prices rose a great deal after the filing.
- **Why the placebo did not catch it.** It redraws dates on the same names, which have the same fat right tail, but a
  random date rarely lands on the two or three events that carry the book. A p of 0.002 here says "the realised
  outliers were lucky relative to random timing", not "13D filings predict returns". With ~1,100 events, the median and
  winsorised columns are the better read, and they say nothing.
- **The filer classifier did not find an edge either.** Fund-like filers (n 399) have a 20-session mean of +1.1%, median
  +0.6%, t 1.44, and -0.5% at 60 sessions. Same-name random dates average -0.7% over 20 sessions (small caps trailed QQQ over
  this window), so the event numbers beat that baseline by about two points, but with the median near zero and no way to separate that from a few large winners.
- **Survivorship is worst here.** Current S&P 400/600 membership tends to follow past success (not checked name by name here), and 13D targets are
  disproportionately small and volatile. Delisted targets (including those acquired after the 13D, which would add a jump)
  and names that fell out of the index are missing, in both directions.
- **Entry is the first close after the filing.** Intraday filings lose the day-0 reaction, which is where the literature
  puts most of the move. This is the tradeable question, but it also means the study cannot test the announcement effect.
- **Crude fund filter.** Keywords on the cover-page name. The first version of this study (and of the live scanner) read only the first
  6,000 characters of each document, but the post-2024 SCHEDULE 13D format puts the cover page ~7,000+ characters in, so 115 of 1,586
  filings had no name and counted as not fund-like. Parsing the whole cached document fixed it (4 unparsed), moved fund-like events
  from 361 to 410 and the primary from t 1.53 to 1.60; the verdict is unchanged. Found 2026-11-09 while smoke-testing the scanner.

## Paper bot: `Activist13DBot` + `sc13dscan` (built 2026-11-09)

Built on request as a forward test, not because the study passed (it did not). Paper only, not in any copier.

- **Scanner** `tradingbot/sc13dscan.py` (CronJob `sc13dscan`, 20:45 UTC on weekdays): reads each submissions JSON of the frozen
  `ACTIVIST_UNIVERSE` (1,093 names, `utils/universes.py`), keeps initial SC 13D / SCHEDULE 13D filings, classifies the filer with the
  study's exact keyword regex (a test pins the two copies together) and writes `sc13d_events`, plus a `_HEARTBEAT` row. The default
  45-day lookback makes the first run seed the whole live book.
- **Bot** `tradingbot/activist13dbot.py` (CronJob `activist13dbot`, 21:15 UTC): holds fund-like targets for 20 sessions, equal weight capped at
  0.5 (the study held 100% of a lone name), 30-day dedupe, first close after the acceptance time. Raises if the scanner is empty or stale.
  The ticker list per run is the last 45 days of fund-like targets plus a never-weighted `QQQ` placeholder.
- **Live smoke test against EDGAR** (scratch SQLite, full universe, 45 days): 269 s, 11 initial 13Ds, 4 fund-like (RXO, ITGR, MAT, BKU), 3 active
  that day. It found two real bugs that unit tests with fixtures had not: requests ran serially (1,829 s) and the cover-page window missed
  every post-2024 filer name (see above). Both are fixed and covered by tests.
- **Expect** `alphareport` to say `too short` for months. At the study's rate (~25 fund-like events a year, 20 sessions each) the book is
  often one to three names or all cash, so its live alpha will be noisy.
